decisions.decision: FileList keeps the Shift-click anchor as a file path, not as a row index. Every click (plain, Ctrl/Cmd, Shift) sets the anchor to the clicked row's path, as today. On Shift-click the anchor path is looked up in the list as it is rendered at that moment (sorted + filtered, the same order selectRange uses); if found, selectRange(anchorIndex, clickedIndex) runs unchanged (the range is still added to the existing selection, as today). If the anchor is null or not in the visible list (hidden by the search, gone after a rescan), the click behaves as today without an anchor: Ctrl/Cmd toggles, otherwise the clicked row alone is selected. The anchor survives metadata updates, D-28 Size/Date refreshes after a save, sort changes and search changes that keep it visible (it follows the item, not the row). The anchor is cleared when the selection becomes empty (open folder, rescan, close folder and Deselect All all clear the selection), so a stale anchor from an earlier scan never extends a range. No store change; selectRange, toggleSelection, setSelectedPaths, selectAll stay as they are. Reference: GTK listview 'Implement extending selections' (mail.gnome.org/archives/commits-list/2020-May/msg13894.html), which imitates Windows Explorer, tracks the base item with an item tracker, not a position. Deviations kept on purpose (B-R21-02, Saba question batch): Shift-click also moves the anchor (Explorer/GTK: only normal clicks set it) and the range is added to the selection (Explorer: Shift without Ctrl replaces it); clearing the anchor on an empty selection also drops it after Ctrl-deselecting the last selected row (an empty selection is the only reliable 'folder content replaced' signal: folderPath does not change on a rescan or when the same folder is reopened)

A schema saved during a pending save therefore survives the save's re-read (fixes A-R21-03). (2) handleSchemaChanged keeps the current store entry of every path whose chunk read rejected instead of dropping it from the metadata map (same rule as D-22 for batch saves); the 'Failed to read N files' toast stays; a selected file whose read failed keeps its form values. D-21..D-32 unchanged. Not part of the K-4 contract (renderer display only) (3) A kept (not re-read) entry does not touch the form: in a single selection setEditingMetadata is called only when the selected path was freshly read (keptPaths guard), so unsaved edits and fields typed during a save (D-30) survive a rejected schema re-read (A-R24-01; the two-part version cleared them, mutant MK-1 killed by (s6)/(s7)). Known consequence (RR-R24-01): a kept entry has no value for a field added by that schema change until the next successful read; the 'Failed to read N files' toast reports it.

Stale-result guard for the schema re-read (renderer only). useFileStore keeps a monotonic writeGeneration and pathWriteGenerations: Record<string, number>; markPathsWritten(paths) increments writeGeneration once and stamps each given path with it. MetadataPanel.handleSave calls it after writeMetadata resolves (single) and after writeMetadataBatch resolves for the succeeded paths only (batch); a rejected write marks nothing. handleSchemaChanged records, for every path in a chunk's result, the writeGeneration read just before that chunk's readMetadataBatch call. When it writes the store (after the last chunk) a path whose pathWriteGenerations value is greater than its recorded generation is superseded: it gets the store entry current at that moment, like a kept path of a rejected chunk. Kept and superseded paths take the store entry current at store-write time (not a snapshot from the reject), are absent if the store has none, and never reset the form (D-33 part 3). Consequence (same class as RR-R24-01): a superseded entry carries the new schema's field only if the save's re-read was issued after the schema change; otherwise the field stays empty until the next successful read. The single-file write in main is synchronous, so without a delay the single-save order is not reachable in production; batch writes yield every 5 files and a multi-chunk re-read spans the save, so the batch and between-chunks orders are reachable. K-4 contract untouched. Deviation from RR-R24-05: handleSave/handleSchemaChanged stay in MetadataPanel (no store action move, RR-R23-04 signal stays open).
decisions.contract_with: none (renderer display and save flow only)

decisions.decision: Stale-result guard for folder reads (renderer only), reusing D-34's write generation. readMetadataChunked(paths, schema, getWriteGeneration: () => number) calls getWriteGeneration() just before each chunk's readMetadataBatch and returns readGenerations: Record<string, number> for every path in that chunk's result (lib stays store-free; callers pass () => useFileStore.getState().writeGeneration). useFileStore.applyMetadataRead(read, readGenerations) replaces metadata like setMetadata, except that a path whose pathWriteGenerations value is greater than its read generation is superseded and gets the store entry current at that moment (absent if none). FolderBrowser handleOpenFolder/handleRescan and App openFolder call it instead of setMetadata on the success path; error paths, empty-folder setMetadata({}) and handleCloseFolder keep setMetadata. The comparison runs at store-write time, so a save that lands between chunks is kept. MetadataPanel (D-34) is not touched. Reachability: single writes are synchronous in main (delay-only); batch writes yield every 5 files and a folder of more than 50 files reads in several chunks, so batch + multi-chunk rescan is reachable. Not covered: a rejected chunk still drops its paths (B-R27-01). Alternative not taken: disabling Rescan/Open Folder during a save (UX, B-R27-02).
decisions.contract_with: none (renderer display and save flow only)

decisions.decision: Folder reads keep the current entry of a rejected chunk (renderer only), the D-33 rule applied to Rescan / Open Folder / drop. readMetadataChunked additionally returns failedPaths: string[] (every path of every rejected chunk, in paths order; failures stays and equals failedPaths.length). useFileStore.applyMetadataRead(read, readGenerations, keptPaths) takes a required third parameter: after the D-35 read loop, every kept path gets the store entry current at store-write time (absent if none); generations, files and selection are untouched. The three callers pass failedPaths and, after applyMetadataRead, show the existing D-33 toast 'Failed to read N files' (error) when failures > 0; no toast when 0. Error paths, the empty-folder setMetadata({}) and handleCloseFolder are unchanged. Open Folder of a different folder: kept paths have no entry and stay absent, the toast reports them. The toast store has one slot, so a later toast can replace it (same as the schema path). Reachability: main catches per-file read errors (emptyMetadata), so a chunk rejects only at IPC level; the consequence fixed is display-only. Not covered: per-file read errors returned as emptyMetadata (RR-R13-01, protected preload).

An empty folder clears the store metadata in all three folder callers (renderer only): FolderBrowser handleOpenFolder and App openFolder (drop) call setMetadata({}) when scanFolder returns no WAV, as handleRescan already does. No toast. Error paths stay as they are and are documented exactly: Open Folder / drop error -> setFiles([]) + setMetadata({}) + toast; Rescan error -> toast only (files and metadata kept). Reason: Close Folder and Open Folder of a non-empty folder already drop the old folder's entries; keeping them on an empty folder let a later rejected read (D-36 keptPaths) show them as current. Display-only.

Folder loads are latest-wins (renderer only). useFileStore gets folderLoadId: number (starts 0, only increases, never reset) and beginFolderLoad(): number (increments and returns the new id); file-store.ts exports isFolderLoadCurrent(loadId). FolderBrowser handleOpenFolder (only after the dialog returned a path, so a cancelled dialog does not cancel the running load), handleRescan and App openFolder take a load id first. After scanFolder resolves, after readMetadataChunked resolves and at the top of catch, a superseded load returns without any store write or toast; finally calls setIsScanning(false) only for the current load. handleCloseFolder calls beginFolderLoad() and setIsScanning(false) in addition to its existing clears, so a pending load cannot repopulate a closed folder and the spinner stops on Close. setFolderPath, clearSelection and the player stop stay synchronous at load start (unchanged). D-35 generations, D-36 keptPaths and D-37 empty-folder clear are unchanged and apply inside the current load. Not covered: the save re-read after a folder switch (RR-R28-03 / RR-R30-01, MetadataPanel) and early stop of a superseded read (B-R30-01).

Late re-reads after a folder switch (renderer only). (a) MetadataPanel handleSave: write, markPathsWritten, the stats refresh, the re-read and every toast stay as they are; the re-read result is written into the store (updateFileMetadata) only for paths still listed in useFileStore.getState().files at that moment (single: if (isListedPath(path)); batch: savedEntries also filtered by isListedPath). Not keyed on folderLoadId: Rescan and same-folder Open Folder also take a load id, and D-35 needs the save's re-read in those cases (B R31 SM-3). Not keyed on folderPath: a parent folder that still lists the file must get the saved value (v5). (b) handleSchemaChanged takes useFileStore.getState().folderLoadId at start; after the chunk loop, if !isFolderLoadCurrent(loadId) it returns: no setMetadata, no editor change, no toast. Any later folder load reads with the new schema already. (c) App openFolder: inside the schema-wait loop, after each 50 ms wait, a superseded load returns (no scan IPC). file-store.ts unchanged; D-34/D-35/D-36/D-37/D-38 unchanged.

Schema re-read waits for a pending folder load (renderer only). MetadataPanel handleSchemaChanged first awaits a module-level waitForFolderLoadIdle(): it resolves at once when useFileStore isScanning is false, otherwise on the first store change where isScanning is false (subscribe, then unsubscribe). Only then it takes files and folderLoadId from useFileStore.getState() (not the render-closure allFiles) and reads those paths with the current schema. The D-39(b) guard, D-33 (rejected chunk keeps the entry, one toast) and D-34 (write-generation keep) are unchanged. Why wait and not skip: a load whose read began before the field was added reads with the old schema; only a re-read after that load lands puts the new field's values in (RR-R32-04). Why not a files-identity guard: a save's stats refresh replaces the files array (updateFileStats) and would drop a valid re-read ((w7)). Effect: Done during a pending load keeps the editor open until the load and the re-read finish (B-R32-01).

An unmounted schema editor never closes the panel (renderer only, SchemaEditor.tsx). SchemaEditor keeps isMountedRef = useRef(false); a mount effect sets it true and its cleanup sets it false (StrictMode-safe). handleSave awaits onSave() and returns without onClose() when isMountedRef.current is false. Why: Back unmounts the editor while Done may still wait (D-40) or re-read; reopening Customize Fields mounts a new editor, and the old Done's onClose (setShowSchemaEditor(false)) would close the new one and drop what the user typed. The pending re-read itself still runs and applies (D-40 unchanged). Done's busy state / re-entrancy is TM-B37.

Schema editor Done busy state (renderer only, SchemaEditor.tsx). A local isApplying state is set on Done; while it is true Done is natively disabled and reads 'Applying...' (same pattern as Save Tags: disabled + 'Saving...', MetadataPanel.tsx:369-372), and the editing area is wrapped in <fieldset disabled={isApplying} className='min-w-0 space-y-4 disabled:opacity-60'>, so no field can be added, removed, toggled or reordered while the re-read runs. Back (header, outside the fieldset) stays enabled: it is the escape and D-41 keeps the pending re-read harmless. If onSave rejects, the editor stays open and isApplying returns to false (no unhandled rejection). Reference: Mp3tag blocks with a 'Writing tag-data' progress dialog; W3C APG list: HTML disabled when the control should not stay focusable. Deviation: native disabled drops focus (GitLab/ARIA posts prefer aria-disabled + aria-busy); kept for consistency with Save Tags and because Back stays focusable

Latest Done wins (renderer only, MetadataPanel.tsx). handleSchemaChanged increments schemaReadIdRef at its start and, after its reads, returns without touching the store when a later handleSchemaChanged has started (checked together with isFolderLoadCurrent). Why: with D-41 a second editor can start a second re-read while the first is pending; the older one landing last overwrote the newer schema's values (QA-R34-01). Known limit B-R34-03 stays: a field added in a reopened editor without pressing Done again is read only if the pending re-read was still waiting for a folder load

useFileStore.setFiles(files) keeps selectedPaths to the paths listed in the new files, in their existing order (renderer only, file-store.ts line 55 + private withListedSelection appended at end). When nothing is pruned the update omits selectedPaths (same array identity); load-start clearSelection, selectRange, selectAll and D-31 anchor rules unchanged. Rejected: clearing on apply (drops a deliberate click on a row the same Rescan still lists). Covers Open Folder, Rescan, drop, scan-reject setFiles([]) and Close Folder. Reference R1-R3 (Qt reset, Kid3, Mp3tag opt-in auto-select), Deviations 1-4 in current-task.md round 37
